title: ESXi / vCenter
description: Are the ESXi hosts overcommitted, and how are datastores filling?

panels.title: Running VMs
panels.description: Powered-on VMs (vCenter has no realtime data for powered-off ones).

panels.title: Memory granted
panels.description: Memory granted to the VMs on the busiest host, as a share of its physical memory. Over 100 % the host is overcommitted and relies on ballooning, compression or swapping; orange from 90 %.

panels.title: vCPU : CPU
panels.description: vCPUs of the running VMs per logical CPU on the busiest host. Up to about 3:1 is usually fine for light workloads; watch CPU ready when it climbs. Orange from 3, red from 5.

targets.expr: max(count by (esxhostname) (vsphere_vm_cpu_ready_summation{cpu!="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"}) / on (esxhostname) count by (esxhostname) (vsphere_host_cpu_usage_average{cpu!="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"}))

panels.title: Worst CPU ready
panels.description: The highest CPU ready time per vCPU across VMs: the share of time a vCPU was ready to run but waited for a physical CPU. Above 5 % per vCPU (orange) VMs feel slow; 10 % is red.

targets.expr: max(max by (esxhostname, vmname) (vsphere_vm_cpu_ready_summation{cpu="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"}) / on (esxhostname, vmname) count by (esxhostname, vmname) (vsphere_vm_cpu_ready_summation{cpu!="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"}) / 20000)

panels.title: Fullest datastore
panels.description: Space used on the fullest datastore. Orange from 80 %, red from 90 %.

panels.title: Hosts
panels.description: Each ESXi host: load, capacity, and how much of it the running VMs claim.

targets.expr: count by (esxhostname) (vsphere_vm_cpu_ready_summation{cpu!="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"}) / on (esxhostname) count by (esxhostname) (vsphere_host_cpu_usage_average{cpu!="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"})

panels.title: Host CPU
panels.description: CPU use of each ESXi host.

panels.title: Host memory
panels.description: Memory each host uses (solid) and the memory granted to its VMs (dashed), as shares of its physical memory.

panels.title: Datastores
panels.description: Space on each datastore. Provisioned counts thin-provisioned disks at their full size, so over 100 % means the datastore can't hold every disk at full size. Full in: at the last week's growth rate.

targets.expr: 1024 * (max by (dsname) (vsphere_datastore_disk_capacity_latest) - max by (dsname) (vsphere_datastore_disk_used_latest)) / clamp_min(1024 * max by (dsname) (deriv(vsphere_datastore_disk_used_latest[7d])), 0.001) / 86400

panels.title: Datastore use
panels.description: Space used on each datastore. vCenter updates datastore figures every 30 minutes.

panels.title: VMs
panels.description: Each running VM. CPU ready is per vCPU: the share of time a vCPU waited for a physical CPU.

targets.expr: max by (vmname, esxhostname, guesthostname, guest, memorySizeMB) (vsphere_vm_cpu_usage_average{cpu="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"})

max by (vmname) (max by (esxhostname, vmname) (vsphere_vm_cpu_ready_summation{cpu="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"}) / on (esxhostname, vmname) count by (esxhostname, vmname) (vsphere_vm_cpu_ready_summation{cpu!="instance-total", esxhostname=~"$esxhost"}) / 20000)

panels.title: VM CPU (top 10)
panels.description: CPU use of the ten busiest VMs.

panels.title: VM memory consumed (top 10)
panels.description: Host memory backing each of the ten largest VMs.
